2. Suparṇa is personified in the yajurveda Saṃhitās as a ṛṣi.
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, iv. 3, 3, 2; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxxix. 7.

Suplan Sārñjaya is the name of a prince of the Sṛñjayas who was taught the dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice by Pratīdarśa, and took the name of sahadeva as a token of his success.
Foot notes Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, ii. 4, 4, 4; xii. 8, 2, 3. Cf. Lévi, La Doctrine du Sacrifice, 139; Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 1, 105, 106.
